hero.title: Slice.js
hero.lede: A component framework built on native Web Components. I design, build and maintain it — and use it to teach how a framework works from the inside.
hero.logoCaption: The framework, its components, its docs and its MCP catalog — one ecosystem.

built.title: A framework, not a demo.
built.description: Slice is a complete toolchain: runtime, CLI, component library, documentation and an MCP catalog.

runtime.title: Runtime
runtime.text: Component lifecycle, props through setters, events, context and a router — built on the platform, not around it.

cli.title: CLI & build
cli.text: Scaffolding, dev server, production bundling, type generation and a doctor command that catches broken projects before deploy.

components.title: Component library
components.text: Visual and Service components with documented APIs, examples and tests; consumed by Conclave and external apps.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: Concepts, guides and API reference written from the source, not from marketing.

mcp.title: MCP catalog
mcp.text: A machine-readable documentation catalog so AI-assisted workflows can query Slice without guessing.

decisions.title: Trade-offs I chose on purpose.
decisions.description: The interesting part of a framework is what it refuses to do. These are the decisions that shape Slice.

platform.title: Native Web Components over a virtual DOM
platform.text: The browser already has a component model. Slice uses it directly instead of shipping a second one.
platform.cost: Cost: less ergonomic than JSX, more explicit boilerplate.

lifecycle.title: Explicit lifecycle over implicit reactivity
lifecycle.text: Constructor, init, update and beforeDestroy are visible. You can read a component and know when it runs.
lifecycle.cost: Cost: more discipline; the framework will not hide the order for you.

buildless.title: Buildless development over bundler-first
buildless.text: ES modules run directly in the browser during development. The CLI is for production, not for every save.
buildless.cost: Cost: more requests in dev and a real build step for production.

registry.title: Docs as a registry + MCP over static pages
registry.text: The documentation is structured data: components, APIs and examples that both humans and agents can query.
registry.cost: Cost: more infrastructure and versioning discipline.
